input: Hello students
We encounter many bridges in our daily lives.
Perhaps it is such an ordinary-looking building
The small bridge, however, bears witness to the passing and experiences of many pedestrians.
Perhaps it is a bridge that not only connects you to your destination
The bridge also adds to the beautiful scenery of your journey.
Therefore, in order to facilitate our systematic and in-depth study of bridge structure-related knowledge...
It is necessary to classify and categorize these various types of bridges.
This is the topic of our lesson today—the classification of bridges.
We can classify bridges from different perspectives.
For example, these bridges
By comparison, it is easy to see that they are built using different materials.
Therefore, we can determine the main load-bearing structure of the bridge.
Classify bridges by the materials used in their construction.
In our country
The most widely used bridge construction material at present is reinforced concrete.
It is worth noting
Currently, some materials with superior performance are already being used in bridge construction.
For example, ultra-high performance concrete is used for the ribs of box arches.
For example, CFRP (carbon fiber reinforced polymer) is used in cable-stayed bridges.
The application of these high-performance materials will further revolutionize bridge engineering.
Let's take a look at these bridges again.
Clearly, they serve different groups of people.

It was built to meet the migration needs of crabs.

The bridge can also be built as a movable bridge.
Previously, we learned about bridge classification based on their intuitive external features.
Next, we will focus on the system classification of bridge structures.
Based on the stress conditions of the bridge's load-bearing structural components
Bridge structural systems can generally be divided into beam bridges.
arch bridge
rigid frame bridge
cable-stayed bridge
Types of suspension bridges
Different bridge structural systems have different stress characteristics.
This further determines the selection of bridge construction materials and the applicable range of bridge spans.
Below, we will briefly introduce the main characteristics of different bridge structural systems.
First, we will study beam bridges.
A beam is erected on the pier.
This results in the simplest bridge type – the simply supported beam bridge.
Beam bridge under vertical load
The support only generates vertical reaction force.
No horizontal reaction force will be generated
The main beam is primarily subjected to bending.
Therefore, we should choose materials with strong bending resistance to construct the main beam.
For example, steel
reinforced concrete, etc.
The structural system of beam bridges can be further subdivided into simply supported beam bridges.
Continuous beam bridge
cantilever bridge
Simply supported beam bridges have simple stress distribution
Construction
Widely used in short-span bridges
Compared to simply supported beams, continuous beams
The main girder of the bridge span forms a continuous structure at the pier top.
Therefore, vehicles pass through more smoothly.
Meanwhile, the main beam at the pier top continuously reinforces the coordinated stress distribution between the adjacent bridge spans.
Currently, it is the most commonly used type of beam bridge in highways and urban roads.
Cantilever bridges have hanging holes between the two cantilever ends.
A relatively complex connection structure needs to be installed at the cantilever end.
This location often becomes a weak point in the bridge structure.
Diseases are very likely to occur.
Affecting bridge performance
Therefore, cantilever bridges are now rarely used.
The main load-bearing structure of an arch bridge is the main arch ring.
Under vertical load
There is horizontal thrust at the arch foot.
The bending moment generated by this thrust on the main arch ring has the opposite sign to the bending moment generated by the vertical load.
Able to cancel each other out
Therefore, the bending moment of the main arch ring
The shear forces are relatively small.
The main arch ring is primarily under compression.
Therefore, for small and medium span arch bridges
It is generally constructed using masonry materials with high compressive strength and reinforced concrete.
For long-span arch bridges
From the perspective of construction stability
From a convenience perspective
It can be constructed using reinforced concrete and steel structures.
Compared with beam bridges of the same span
Due to the bending moment of the main arch ring
Both shear force and deformation are very small.
Therefore, arch bridges have a great spanning capacity.
The arch bridge currently under construction has a span exceeding 600 meters.
Where conditions permit
Building arch bridges is often an economically reasonable choice.
At the same time, the arched bridge has a more aesthetically pleasing curved shape.
certainly
The curved shape of the arch bridge also makes its construction more difficult than that of the beam bridge.
in addition
The horizontal thrust at the arch foot of a through-arch bridge places high demands on the bearing capacity of the foundation.
As for the under-arch bridge
Tie rods can be installed at the arch foot.
To balance the thrust of the arch feet
This reduces the requirements for the bearing capacity of the foundation.
This type of arch bridge is also known as a "tied arch bridge".
The main load-bearing structure of a rigid frame bridge is a rigid frame structure in which beams and piers are integrally combined.
The biggest difference between it and a beam bridge lies in the structural treatment of the pier-beam connection.
After the piers and beams are fixed together
The piers of the rigid frame bridge will also participate in the bending of the main beam.
This has a certain effect on improving the bending resistance of the bridge span.
Commonly used rigid frame bridge types include portal rigid frame bridges.
Inclined-leg rigid frame bridges and continuous rigid frame bridges
Portal rigid frame bridge under vertical load
The bridge span structure, like a beam bridge, is subjected to bending moment.
However, because the bridge piers impose rotational constraints on the main beam...
The mid-span bending moment is smaller than that of a simply supported beam with the same span.
Therefore, the height of the bridge structure can be made smaller (3)
The horizontal constraint of the foundation on the pier foot will generate thrust.
This horizontal thrust can generate axial pressure on the main beam.
Therefore, the stress state of its portal rigid frame bridge is between that of a beam bridge and an arch bridge.
The bridge piers bear both vertical pressure and bending moment.
At the pier-beam fixed position
Due to the high structural stiffness
Therefore, the negative bending moment is also relatively large if ordinary reinforced concrete is used for construction.
This area is prone to cracking.
Portal rigid frame bridges in temperature
Under non-uniform foundation settlement
It will generate relatively large additional secondary internal forces in the structure.
inclined leg rigid frame bridge
As the name suggests
It means making the bridge piers at an angle.
This structural feature can increase the spanning space under the bridge.
Make the bridge design light and beautiful
However, the construction of the slanted legs will be more difficult.
Continuous rigid frame bridges are a type of long-span bridge commonly used in mountainous terrain in Yunnan Province.
It belongs to a multi-statically indeterminate structure.
Therefore, the secondary internal force effect will be more severe.
In order to mitigate the adverse effects of secondary internal force
The piers of continuous rigid frame bridges are generally made to be more flexible.
Forming a high-pier, long-span continuous rigid frame bridge
Next, we will learn about cable-stayed bridges.
A cable-stayed bridge includes cable stays.
Main beam
The three main components of the tower column
Due to the presence of the stay cables
Significant changes in the stress on the bridge structure
Without the effect of the stay cables
So the main beam is in Heng
Under live vertical load
The bridge structure is designed as a three-span continuous beam.
Let's add the bridge towers and cables to examine the stress changes in the structure.
At this point, the cable is pulled upwards.
Lift the main beam at multiple points
It's like having a series of "invisible bridge piers".
The vertical components of the stay cables provide multi-point vertical elastic support for the main beam.
This significantly improves the bending moment of the main beam.
Reduce the self-weight of the main beam
This would significantly increase the bridge's spanning capacity.
The main span of the world's largest cable-stayed bridge currently exceeds 1100m.
One thing to note
With the increase in bridge span
The weight of the stay cables will produce a sag effect.
This leads to a decrease in the stiffness of cable-stayed bridges.
This is a major reason limiting the increase in the span of cable-stayed bridges.
The horizontal component of the stay cables will exert an axial compressive force on the main girder pointing towards the bridge tower.
